categories.template: The robot has a circular body with radius {r_m} m and height 1.5 m. From the current first-person view, suppose it moves straight forward without turning. Before first physical contact within the visible local space, approximately how far can it move? A. less than 2 body-widths B. 2 to 4 body-widths C. 4 to 8 body-widths D. more than 8 body-widths
categories.gt_rule: Use only matched real R2R frame triplets from rgb/depth/pose/*.json, joined by scan_id, episode_id, and frame_id; never synthesize image paths or labels. Back-project depth with intrinsics and pose into an ego ground frame with x=lateral, z=forward, y=height above ground. Remove floor points with y<=0.05 m, keep candidate body-blocking evidence in 0.05<y<=1.50 m, and reject overhang, glass/mirror, thin-obstacle, off-screen, hidden-dependent, or ambiguous frames. Use a visibility support grid with 0.05 m longitudinal and lateral spacing over the swept corridor; reject if valid supported cells over the decisive segment are <0.70 or if any contiguous unsupported centerline run exceeds 0.30 m. For radius r and theta=0, require a legal start pose with no body-band obstacle inside the initial disk plus 0.02 m tolerance, then sweep a ground-plane disk/capsule corridor. For each obstacle point p, compute longitudinal s and lateral l in the action frame; if abs(l)<=r, first center contact distance is s - sqrt(max(0, r*r-l*l)); the minimum nonnegative contact distance is d_safe_m. Project collision points to RGB and mark collision_point_visible only if the pixel is inside image bounds with at least 8 px margin and has valid depth support within 0.15 m in a 5x5 neighborhood. Convert to d_safe_bw=d_safe_m/(2r). Bin by [2,4,8] only if distance to the nearest bin edge is >=0.5 body-widths; for >8 require no visible contact and visible corridor support through 8.5 body-widths. Require label stability under nuisance perturbations: yaw +/-2 deg, depth scale +/-1 percent, floor threshold +/-0.02 m, obstacle min-height +/-0.02 m, and visibility grid size in {0.04,0.05,0.06} m; accepted manifest stability must be >=95 percent. Emit scan_id, episode_id, rgb_path, depth_path, pose_path, d_safe_m, d_safe_bw, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, bin_margin_body_widths, flip_pair_id=null, oracle_trace_path, and overlay_path. Enforce category max answer share<=0.40, and for any radius subgroup with n>=8 enforce max answer share<=0.40. Require at least 5 scans and 10 episodes, max scan share<=0.35, and max episode share<=0.20.

categories.template: The robot has a circular body with radius {r_m} m and height 1.5 m. From the current first-person view, suppose it turns {theta_abs} degrees to the {left_or_right} and then moves forward {H_bw} body-widths. Within the visible local space, will any part of its body make physical contact? A. yes, it will collide B. no, it can complete the motion without contact
categories.gt_rule: Use the common R2R rgb/depth/pose/*.json loader and oracle constants from Forward Body Clearance. Theta is defined in the ego ground frame with negative=left-front and positive=right-front; the hypothetical turn sets only the translation direction. Use theta in {-30,-15,15,30} and H_bw in {2,4}; H_m=H_bw*(2r). Label A only when d_safe_bw<=H_bw-0.5 and collision_point_visible=true. Label B only when no contact occurs through H_bw and visible corridor support extends through H_bw+0.5 body-widths. Reject abs(d_safe_bw-H_bw)<0.5, visible_sweep_ratio<0.70, requires_hidden_geometry=true, ambiguous evidence, illegal starts, hidden-dependent evidence, or unstable perturbation labels. Emit scan_id, episode_id, rgb_path, depth_path, pose_path, theta, H_bw, d_safe_m, d_safe_bw, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, bin_margin_body_widths, flip_pair_id=null, oracle_trace_path, and overlay_path. Enforce category max answer share<=0.65, and for any subgroup with n>=8 enforce max answer share<=0.65 by radius, theta, H_bw, and theta x H_bw. Require at least 5 scans and 10 episodes, max scan share<=0.35, and max episode share<=0.20.

categories.template: The robot has a circular body with radius {r_m} m and height 1.5 m. From the current view, compare left-front 30 degrees, straight forward, and right-front 30 degrees. Which direction allows the longest movement before first physical contact within the visible local space? A. left-front 30 degrees B. straight forward C. right-front 30 degrees
categories.answer_format: A/B/C mapped to left-front, straight, right-front
categories.gt_rule: Use the common R2R rgb/depth/pose/*.json loader and oracle constants from Forward Body Clearance. Compute d_safe_bw for theta=-30,0,+30 with negative=left-front and positive=right-front. Use shared visible_eval_horizon_bw=8; cap no-contact distances at 8 only after validating visible corridor support through the capped segment. All three corridors must have visible_sweep_ratio>=0.70, requires_hidden_geometry=false, no off-screen or around-corner decisive evidence, legal start, and stable oracle label. Label the unique argmax of capped visible distance only if top1-top2>=0.5 body-widths. Reject capped ties, hidden-dependent winners, near ties, and any case where a finite contact point used in the comparison is not visible. Emit scan_id, episode_id, rgb_path, depth_path, pose_path, per_direction_d_safe_bw, per_direction_visible_sweep_ratio, visible_sweep_ratio=min over directions, collision_point_visible=all finite comparison contacts visible, requires_hidden_geometry=false, bin_margin_body_widths=top1-top2, flip_pair_id=null, oracle_trace_path, and overlay_path. Enforce category max answer share<=0.48, and for any radius subgroup with n>=8 enforce max answer share<=0.48. Require at least 5 scans and 10 episodes, max scan share<=0.35, and max episode share<=0.20.

categories.template: In the same first-person view, compare two circular robot bodies: Robot S has radius {r_small_m} m. Robot L has radius {r_large_m} m. If both move {direction_text} for the same distance of {distance_m} m from the current position, which statement is correct within the visible local space? A. both can complete the motion without contact B. only Robot S can complete the motion without contact C. neither can complete the motion without contact
categories.answer_format: A=both-safe, B=small-only, C=neither-safe; no only-large-safe target
categories.gt_rule: Use the same real R2R rgb/depth/pose/*.json frame, same action theta, and same metric distance_m for both bodies. Use r_small=0.10 m and r_large=0.40 m for the primary counterfactual pair; use theta in {-30,0,+30} with negative=left-front, zero=straight, and positive=right-front. Choose distance_m from the fixed grid {0.8,1.2,1.6,2.0,2.4} m and keep at most one accepted distance per frame/action/label by maximum threshold margin. Compute d_safe_m for both radii using the common oracle constants from Forward Body Clearance. A body completes the motion only if d_safe_m>=distance_m and visible free-corridor support extends through distance_m+0.5*(2r) for that body; a body fails only if d_safe_m<=distance_m-0.5*(2r) with visible collision evidence. Label A if both complete, B if only Robot S completes, and C if neither completes; discard any only-large outcome as oracle_error. Require legal starts for both radii, metric monotonicity d_safe_m(r_small)>=d_safe_m(r_large) within one oracle sampling step, visible large collision for B, sufficient small-body visible corridor evidence, visible_sweep_ratio=min over both decisive corridors >=0.70, requires_hidden_geometry=false, ambiguous=false, and stable label under nuisance perturbations. Emit scan_id, episode_id, rgb_path, depth_path, pose_path, theta, direction_text, distance_m, d_safe_m_small, d_safe_m_large, flip_pair_id, monotonicity_status, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, bin_margin_body_widths=min per-body normalized margin, oracle_trace_path, and overlay_path. For target_per_category=30, require at least 10 small-only flip cases, at least 8 both-safe controls, and at least 8 neither-safe controls; if target_per_category changes, require small-only >=ceil(0.33*target) and each no-flip label >=ceil(0.25*target). Enforce category max answer share<=0.48, and for any subgroup with n>=8 enforce max answer share<=0.48 by theta/action, distance_m, body-pair, and theta x distance_m. Require a distance-only baseline report and reject quantitative use if distance-only approaches RGB model performance. Require at least 5 scans and 10 episodes, max scan share<=0.35, and max episode share<=0.20.

categories.template: The robot has a circular body with radius {r_m} m and height 1.5 m. From the current view, suppose it moves straight forward within the visible local space for up to {H_bw} body-widths. If its body makes physical contact, in which region of the image would the first contact occur? A. lower-left B. lower-center C. lower-right D. no visible contact within this motion
categories.answer_format: A/B/C/D mapped to lower-left, lower-center, lower-right, no visible contact
categories.gt_rule: Use the common R2R rgb/depth/pose/*.json loader and oracle constants from Forward Body Clearance with theta=0 and diagnostic H_bw=8. For contact labels, require d_safe_bw<=7.5, collision_point_visible=true, projected collision_point_pixel in the lower image band (pixel y >= 0.50 image height), at least 5 percent image width margin from lower-left/lower-center/lower-right bucket boundaries, and stable region assignment under the nuisance perturbation suite. Label D only when there is no visible contact within H_bw=8 and visible corridor support extends through 8.5 body-widths. Reject hidden-dependent, off-screen, overhang, ambiguous, illegal-start, or visibility-failing cases. Accept only visible_sweep_ratio>=0.70 and requires_hidden_geometry=false. Emit scan_id, episode_id, rgb_path, depth_path, pose_path, collision_point_pixel, region_margin_px, visible_sweep_ratio, collision_point_visible, requires_hidden_geometry, bin_margin_body_widths, flip_pair_id=null, oracle_trace_path, and overlay_path. Keep optional and out of the core survival gate. If reported quantitatively, enforce category max answer share<=0.40 and for any radius or H_bw subgroup with n>=8 enforce max answer share<=0.40.
